summary: Builds the single-file self-contained HTML notebook browser and writes it to .coldstart/notebook/index.html (kbView), and keeps index.html gitignored inside the notebook dir. The non-obvious constraint, and the reason the write is content-conditional as of 2026-07-24: kbView is NOT only the user's explicit `kb view` command — the keeper calls it after EVERY cache save via refreshKbNotesIndex -> regenerateKbViewIfPresent, so a plain code edit with no note involved used to re-render and rewrite this file and bump its mtime all day. The skip-if-identical check is safe specifically because `generated` is a date stamp (sliced to 10 chars by the caller), not a clock stamp, so identical notes really do render identical bytes; a clock-stamped value here would silently defeat it.

summary: Builds the single-file self-contained HTML notebook browser written to .coldstart/notebook/index.html (kbView). Verified this session in buildViewData/toClientNote: the note-to-note links the view can draw come ONLY from hand-typed [[wikilinks]] scraped out of each note's markdown body (outLinks), and backlinks are just the reverse of those — the anchors array (the file paths every note already carries) is stamped for freshness and used for the dir grouping, but contributes NO edges. That is why the rendered graph is nearly empty on a real notebook (101 notes produced 7 links / 9 visible nodes): the connective tissue that exists is anchors, and the graph does not read it. Also still true and easy to break: kbView is not only the explicit `kb view` command — the keeper calls it after every cache save, so the write is content-conditional, and that skip-if-identical check is only safe because `generated` is a date stamp rather than a clock stamp.

summary: Builds the baked JSON for `kb view` and writes/opens the notebook's index.html. The non-obvious part is linkByAnchor: the note graph used to draw ONLY hand-typed [[wikilinks]], and agents write almost none — on this repo that was 8 links across 108 notes, so the graph showed nine nodes. It now also links any two notes that anchor the same file, capped at 8 per note ordered by how many files they share, because one hub file with twenty notes on it is a 190-edge clique that says nothing. The write is content-conditional and `generated` is date-stamped rather than clock-stamped so identical notes render identical bytes; the keeper re-renders this file after every cache save, which means a stale dist/ will silently overwrite a freshly generated page until the keeper is restarted.

summary: Builds the baked JSON for `kb view` and writes/opens the notebook's index.html. linkByAnchor draws graph edges between any two notes that anchor the same file (capped at 8/note), on top of hand-typed [[wikilinks]], because agents write almost no wikilinks on their own. `renderViewHtml` now also substitutes `<!--__HOME_LINK__-->` with '' this session, mirroring `src/graph/view.ts`'s `renderGraphHtml` — the standalone `kb view` CLI page has nowhere to link back to, so only the website build script (`scripts/kb-viewer/build-site-page.mjs`) fills the placeholder in, and only by substituting into the raw template BEFORE this function runs.
